Chapter 1: The Twenties as a Crucial Foundation for Adult Life
So, let’s talk about your twenties. You’ve probably heard people say this decade is just for experimenting, drifting, or putting off big decisions. Maybe you’ve been told it’s the time to “find yourself” and that real life doesn’t start until later. Sound familiar?
Well, here’s something important—this way of thinking actually misses how the habits and choices you make in your twenties quietly set the stage for everything that comes next. Your twenties aren’t just a waiting room for your “real” adult life. They’re the foundation where your future relationships, your career, and even your sense of self start to take shape.
What makes this period so unique? For the first time, you’re really steering your own ship. There’s a new sense of freedom, but also a growing responsibility. The things you do—good or bad—start to add up. And here’s a cool fact: your brain’s still changing and adapting, thanks to something called neuroplasticity. That means you’re primed for learning, growth, and picking up new habits that tend to stick with you long after.
Think about it like building a house. Your twenties are when you pour the foundation. If you take the time to make it solid and thoughtful, everything you build on top will be stronger and easier to maintain. But if you cut corners or ignore it, fixing things later gets a whole lot tougher. Don’t worry—no one expects perfection, and mistakes aren’t the end of the world. What really matters is being intentional, making small, steady investments in yourself, and your future self will thank you for it.
There’s a myth out there that you’ll “figure it all out” later, that you’ve got endless time. And yes, life is long and you can always change course, but the options you’ll have down the road often depend on the groundwork you lay right now. Careers start to take shape, friendships become more settled, and some opportunities—like starting a family or going back to school—can get trickier as time goes on.
It’s also totally normal to feel anxious or uncertain during these years. The pressure to “get it right” can feel overwhelming, and sometimes it’s tempting to avoid making decisions altogether. But here’s the thing: not choosing is still a choice. And staying stuck can actually close off future options. Learning to live with uncertainty and move forward anyway—that’s a huge part of growing into adulthood.
So, if you take one thing away from this, let it be this: your twenties are far from a throwaway decade. They’re a defining chapter, packed with potential to shape the rest of your life. Seeing it this way isn’t meant to add pressure—it’s meant to empower you, to help you engage with this time proactively, instead of just waiting for “real life” to begin.
